name: CIV
label: Revelation
lede: Three-quarters of Gorilla Biscuits, a songwriter who wasn't in the band, a homemade video that made it to Buzz Bin, and a debut that took a New York hardcore band into MTV's Buzz Bin.

eras.title: Gorilla Biscuits under another name
eras.text: Gorilla Biscuits had broken up, and Walter Schreifels was busy making heavy records with Quicksand. He still had fast, funny, hooky songs in him, and he knew exactly which friends should play them. The band got named after its singer.

years.h: Civarelli, Smilios and Siegler regroup as CIV
years.p: Singer [[Anthony Civarelli|a5d69704-924b-4128-9577-e16531503890]] and bassist [[Arthur Smilios|40d4f905-3bb1-4d2e-9a9b-1d7891033094]] come from Gorilla Biscuits, joined by drummer [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]] (ex-[[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]]) and guitarist [[Charlie Garriga|4f24f7e7-bc37-45d1-8f60-99bc992cd780]]. They name the band CIV, after Civarelli.
years.xp:
Arthur Smilios had finished school and missed playing. Walter Schreifels, whose band [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]] had signed to a major, reunited a late version of Gorilla Biscuits around songs he'd written.

Why not just call it Gorilla Biscuits? Schreifels said he wanted freedom to try new things and be funnier, without hardcore's owners' manual hanging over it.

years.h: Walter Schreifels writes CIV's songs without joining
years.p: Walter Schreifels writes most of CIV's debut, Set Your Goals, and co-produces it with [[Don Fury|0bec484f-b890-4823-af64-0e48530f6f6f]] from 1994 into 1995. It's a break from Quicksand's weight: hardcore songs that aren't heavy.

eras.title: Buzz Bin
eras.text: CIV, a hardcore band from the Revelation family, landed on the Atlantic imprint Lava, made a video for Can't Wait One Minute More for almost nothing, and ended up on MTV and on Beavis and Butt-head. It was about as far into the mainstream as a band out of the NYHC matinees had gone.

years.p: Lava, the Atlantic imprint run by Jason Flom, signs CIV. Arthur Smilios said later he would have stayed independent.

CIV's debut, produced by Don Fury and Walter Schreifels, reaches No. 11 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and No. 184 on the Billboard 200. A Bay Area band later names itself [[Set Your Goals|03d8f83e-a647-4bde-968a-189c0f147783]] after it.
years.xp: Michael Barbiero mixed Set Your Goals. The singles also came out on Revelation vinyl.

q: We made the video ourselves and it got on MTV.
years.h: CIV's homemade Can't Wait One Minute More video hits MTV
years.p: Can't Wait One Minute More, with [[Lou Koller|f1549cac-a48c-4741-8edd-09c1016ada64]] of [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]] on guest vocals, gets a talk-show-parody video directed by Marcos Siega. It goes into MTV's Buzz Bin, onto Beavis and Butt-head, and to No. 21 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks.
years.xp:
Walter Schreifels called it the best pairing of song and video he ever had, and he meant the cheapness as praise. Choices Made got a video too.

Can't Wait One Minute More kept turning up for a decade: a Nissan commercial around 2005, What's New, Scooby-Doo?, Mega Man and Road Rash 3D.

years.h: CIV on the soundtrack to John Carpenter's Escape from L.A.
years.p: CIV lands on the soundtrack to Escape from L.A.. More singles follow on Lava and Atlantic.

eras.title: The getaway
eras.text: CIV's second album, Thirteen Day Getaway, came without Walter Schreifels as the main writer, with new producers, and was dedicated to Warzone singer Raybeez, who died in 1997. It split critics hard, and by 2000 CIV had called a halt.

years.h: Arthur Smilios leaves CIV; Cache Tolman joins
years.p: Arthur Smilios leaves before CIV's second album, Thirteen Day Getaway, is finished; [[Cache Tolman|1d48168d-10f9-48f7-9cb9-622f1a0e39c1]] comes in on bass. Walter Schreifels contributes a single song this time.
Ray Barbieri, [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]]'s singer and a fixture of the CBGB matinees, dies of complications from pneumonia at 35. CIV dedicates Thirteen Day Getaway to him.

q: It was a great record that was about a decade ahead of its time.
years.p: CIV's second album, produced by Michael Barbiero, John Goodmanson and Steve Thompson, and dedicated to Ray "Raybeez" Barbieri. Reviews run from a 1.0 at Pitchfork to a 7.5 at Germany's Rock Hard.
years.xp:
The Plain Dealer heard one more post-[[Green Day|084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19]] band. The San Diego Union-Tribune heard pop hooks with a punk charge. Nobody heard the same record.

Arthur Smilios, who'd left before it was done, has defended it ever since.

years.p: The single from CIV's Thirteen Day Getaway, released a month after the album.
After two albums, Set Your Goals and Thirteen Day Getaway, CIV announces a permanent hiatus.

eras.title: Goals, revisited
eras.text: The reunions came as one-offs, each built around an occasion: a hardcore bowling-alley weekend, a Belgian festival, a New York ballroom. Nobody announced a new album.

years.h: CIV reunites at the Black N Blue Bowl
years.p: CIV plays the Black N Blue Bowl hardcore weekend, its first show since the 2000 hiatus.
The Belgian festival Groezrock puts CIV back on a big stage.
CIV headlines Webster Hall on East 11th Street in New York.

eras.title: Sharing a bill with Shelter
eras.text: Sammy Siegler had been back in Shelter since 2018. In 2024 CIV and Shelter went out together.

years.h: CIV tours with Shelter, then plays the Netherlands
years.p: CIV plays a run with [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]] and a show in the Netherlands.

sources.title: Rest Assured: R.I.P. Raybeez, Nov 27 1961 – Sept 11 1997
